column1: # MODES.tsv — WHICH INSTRUMENT GRADES AN ENTRY IN THIS PACKAGE. name<TAB>modes<TAB># the MEASUREMENT that put it here.
# modes is m3, m4, or m3,m4. An entry not named here is graded in BOTH modes: this file is opt-in, and a
# missing row is never a guess. ⛔ A ROW IS NOT AN EXCLUSION. A declared entry stays in SHIPPED and in
# GRADED and keeps its place in the published denominator; the declaration says only which arm can answer
# the question, and test_icon_jcon_suite.sh NAMES every not-graded cell on its board so a smaller per-mode
# TOTAL can never read as a silent drop. ⛔ A ROW NAMING NO SHIPPED PROGRAM REFUSES THE RUNNER rc=2: a
# declaration that outlives the file it declares is the decay class this fleet keeps paying for.
# ⛔ CARRY THE MEASUREMENT, NEVER JUST THE MODE (ceo CEO-561, adopting this seat's standing practice: a wrong
# exclusion costs more than a wrong cure, because a red stays visible and an excluded name cannot be red).
# A future seat reading a bare "m3" will try to "fix" it back to m3,m4 and re-open a settled question.
# ⛔⭐ THE kwds ROW IS RETIRED, 2026-09-11, hq_V, ON A MEASUREMENT AND NOT ON A PREFERENCE (ceo CEO-581).
# It read: kwds m3 -- "no better ref and no pinned name can fix m4 against a one-step ref", CEO-561's own words
# and TRUE OF THE REF MODEL AS IT STOOD. Two things changed under it. (1) The m4 invocation is now PINNED to a
# stated name (./kwds, hq_V 2026-09-11), so the answer no longer changes between runs and a ref can be cut from
# it at all. (2) CEO-581 ruled the REF MODEL itself: MODES MAY DIVERGE has been law since 2026-08-28 and each
# mode is graded against the oracle INDEPENDENTLY, so a line whose value the INVOCATION determines gets ONE REF
# PER MODE -- see kwds.moderef, whose receipt carries the oracle run under both invocations. MEASURED HERE
# BEFORE THE ROW WAS REMOVED, on a one-program scratch corpus, both arms: with kwds.moderef m3 PASS and m4 PASS;
# without it m3 PASS and m4 FAIL. The entry is graded in BOTH arms again, which is a cell given BACK to the
# denominator -- the opposite of the direction a declaration file usually moves. This file is now empty of rows
# and that is the correct state: it is opt-in, and nothing in this package needs it today.
